Burnette is the only Kodiak AI insider buying

Founder, CEO and Director Don Burnette is the only insider at Kodiak AI to have stepped in on the market over the past year, which puts his recent trade in clear view because no other director or executive joined him on the buy side.

That purchase followed Kodiak AI’s early November quarterly report, which showed higher sales than the same period a year earlier and a swing from a loss to a profit for the quarter, so the trade landed soon after a period when the business had just updated investors on how operations were tracking. Over the three months since Burnette bought, the shares have moved so that the $2.2m insiders spent on shares is now worth about $2.5m, and the shares now trade 11% above Don Burnette's average purchase price, which means the buyers as a group paid less than today's price and the market has moved their way since.

Read together, this reflects a single insider choosing to add to an existing position, with no follow-on from other insiders. The activity points to confidence from Burnette rather than a broader signal from the rest of the leadership team.

Driverless freight fleets need to scale for Kodiak AI

For Burnette’s buying to work out, Kodiak AI needs its Driver as a Service freight model to turn contracted fleets into steady, higher margin revenue. There have been no new public milestones since the November 24, 2026 trade, although the share price has moved above the level insiders paid.

The single insider buy at Kodiak AI sits against a register where insiders together own 21.9% of the company, a stake worth $55.1m at today’s price and typical for a micro-cap. Their decisions involve real exposure but do not dominate the free float. Founder Don Burnette, who made the trade, is also the largest holder with 13.4% of the company, so the purchase was a call on a sizeable personal position. Paz Eshel is the second-largest holder with 5.9% of the company and cut their holding by 29% in a filing dated September 30, 2026.
